sections.h2: Ways to sell and move on in Davie
sections.html:
Selling in Davie breaks down into an agent, a do-it-yourself sale, or a buyer who pays cash and takes on the repairs. Match the choice to the condition of the house and how urgently you need the proceeds.

The town looks and behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Many lots have barns, fencing, pools or other outbuildings, and an inspector will flag those extras, so plan for them from the first day.

  • Agent: widest reach, with open houses, a lender's appraisal and a financing contingency to get through.
  • Owner sale: contract, disclosures and closing coordination all land on you.
  • Cash buyer: no lender involved, often picked for estate homes, rentals and houses in poor shape.

sections.h2: Western Theme rules and lot types
sections.html:
Davie describes itself as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown, and it has more than 107,000 residents. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage. Check with the Town on whether it reaches exterior work on your parcel, especially inside the western-themed district.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Sort out roof age, pool condition and outbuildings before showings begin.

If an association covers your property, request its governing documents early. In many communities a sale needs association approval, estoppel letters and a check for pending special assessments. A late answer from the association can stall a closing longer than a repair would.

Davie regulates short stays through a registration program. The Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and Florida Statutes section 509.242 define a vacation rental as a unit let to transient guests on more than three occasions in a year, each for under thirty days, or one advertised as regularly let that way.

A state DBPR license must be in hand before the Town will take your application. The packet also wants proof of ownership pulled from the county appraiser, corporate papers if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

A violation can bring a civil penalty of up to $500. Call the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before you advertise.

sections.h2: Offices and records you will need
sections.html:
A Davie seller can get most of the records needed from three places. Vacation rental registration and code questions go to the Police Code Compliance Division, 1230 South Nob Hill Road, phone 954-693-8237. Proof of ownership comes from BCPA.net, the Broward appraiser's website. Where an LLC or corporation holds title, the Town wants corporate documents from Sunbiz.org.

Gather them before a buyer's attorney asks. A clean ownership record, a recent tax bill and written word that no code case is open all make the contract easier to sign.

One more item matters to a disabled veteran. The Town's rental program asks for a DD214 and disability papers before applying a veteran exemption, and those same papers support any question a buyer raises about the state's assessment reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers.

sections.h2: Broward property taxes and the sale
sections.html:
Your Davie property is valued and billed by Broward County on the state's schedule. Value is fixed on January 1, a notice of proposed taxes arrives in August, and the bill follows in November.

  • Exemptions and classifications must be filed by March 1, which is important for a lot with an agricultural classification.
  • Petitions on value go to the clerk in the 25 days following the August notice.
  • Paying early earns 4 percent in November, shrinking to 1 percent in February.
  • April 1 is when delinquency starts.

Without homestead, assessed value can climb no more than 10 percent a year. A homestead gets the Save Our Homes cap, the smaller of 3 percent or the change in inflation. Selling ends the cap and the buyer starts from just value.

Land with an agricultural classification deserves a call to the appraiser about how a sale or a change in use affects it, ideally before you sign anything.

Deeds are recorded by the Broward clerk, and the state stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Under the statute, a mortgage or other encumbrance on the land counts toward consideration whether or not the buyer assumes it. Paying off your loan therefore does not shrink the tax base, as some sellers hope.

Liability for the tax is shared by every party. The contract decides who pays, and the title company normally collects it.

Recording fees are separate. Section 28.24 charges $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with records-fund and technology charges per page. Exemptions are listed for spousal homestead deeds and for divorce deeds on the marital home, so check with your title agent before assuming tax is due.

Florida law gives each of these a defined path, and a sale stays possible.

If an heir is selling, a personal representative's deed made under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable. A transfer for estate planning is taxable, since no specific exemption covers it. Florida has charged no estate tax on deaths after December 31, 2004.

The clerk's sale after a foreclosure judgment is set for 20 to 35 days out, unless the plaintiff agrees to extend it. A buyer who closes ahead of that date pays off the lender and leaves you any equity.

For unpaid rent the landlord serves a three-day written demand, leaving out weekends and court holidays. Should a tenant raise a defense other than payment, the rent must be deposited with the court within five days, or the defenses are lost.

Request a lender payoff letter, decide who will hold the keys, and get a draft settlement statement from the title agent shortly before closing. Check it against your contract line by line so a mismatch surfaces early. Bring photo ID, and save a copy of everything you sign. After closing, forward your new address to the tax collector and your insurer, and cancel your homeowner's policy only once the deed has been recorded.

faqs.q: Does Davie require registration for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

faqs.q: What is the Davie vacation rental fee?
faqs.a: A full registration year runs $500 and the half year from April 1 runs $300. Renewals cost $450 when the owner does not live there and $400 when the owner does.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a Davie property?
faqs.a: The Broward clerk records it and takes the deed stamp tax of 70 cents per $100, and the title company usually arranges both.

faqs.q: What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?
faqs.a: The cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida homestead? Ask the Broward appraiser about portability.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer may accept the lease as written. For a vacant house, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and only a sheriff can physically remove an occupant.
